title: Rotational motion
competency: Describe rotation with angular displacement, velocity and acceleration, use the rotational equations and relate them to linear motion.

keywords.def: The angle a body turns through, Δθ = θ_f − θ₀, in radians.
How fast the angle changes: ω = Δθ/Δt, in rad/s.
How fast the angular velocity changes: α = Δω/Δt, in rad/s².
Angular velocity changes by the same amount every second.
The velocity of a point on a turning body, along the tangent to its circle: v = ωr.
The rate of change of tangential speed: a = rα.

en.text: In a rigid body every particle turns through the same angle. Angular displacement Δθ is measured in radians (1 rev = 2π rad = 360°). Angular velocity ω = Δθ/Δt in rad/s; angular acceleration α = Δω/Δt in rad/s². The direction of ω follows the right-hand rule; α points along ω when speeding up and opposite when slowing down.

am.text: በጠንካራ አካል ሁሉም ቅንጣቶች እኩል ማዕዘን ይዞራሉ። ω = Δθ/Δt (rad/s)፣ α = Δω/Δt (rad/s²)። 1 ዙር = 2π ራዲያን = 360°።

screens.title: Rotation of a rigid body
paras: A rigid body keeps its shape as it turns.
Every particle moves in a circle around the axis.
All particles turn through the same angle.

screens.title: Angular velocity and acceleration
paras: Average angular velocity: ω = Δθ/Δt, in rad/s.
Average angular acceleration: α = Δω/Δt, in rad/s².
Right-hand rule: curl your fingers with the rotation. Your thumb points along ω.
Speeding up: α points the same way as ω.
Slowing down: α points opposite to ω.

screens.why: rpm (revolutions per minute) measures angular velocity, not an angle.

screens.ask: A wheel speeds up from 30 rad/s to 50 rad/s in 2 s. Its average angular acceleration is ___ rad/s²

screens.why: ω_av = (30 + 50)/2 = 40 rad/s. (The book's Example 2.5 asks for this but computes α.)

screens.ask: The second hand of a clock has ω ≈ ___ rad/s (3 decimal places)

screens.clue: How long is one turn of the second hand?

screens.text: A wheel turns counterclockwise in the xy plane and is slowing down. α points along
screens.why: ω is along +z (right-hand rule); slowing down makes α opposite: −z.

ideas.name: Equations of rotation with constant α

en.text: With constant angular acceleration the rotation equations copy the linear ones: replace s by θ, v by ω and a by α. So ω_f = ω₀ + αt, Δθ = ω₀t + ½αt², ω_f² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ and ω_av = (ω₀ + ω_f)/2. Angles must be in radians.

am.text: ቋሚ α ሲኖር የመዞሪያ እኩልታዎች ከቀጥታ እንቅስቃሴ ጋር ይመሳሰላሉ፡ ω_f = ω₀ + αt፣ Δθ = ω₀t + ½αt²፣ ω_f² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ።

en.text: A point at distance r from the axis moves along an arc s = rθ. Its tangential speed is v = ωr and its tangential acceleration is a = rα. Every point has the same ω and α, but points farther out move faster. θ must be in radians.

am.text: ከዘንጉ r ርቀት ላይ ያለ ነጥብ s = rθ ይጓዛል፤ v = ωr፣ a = rα። ሁሉም ነጥቦች እኩል ω አላቸው፤ ሩቅ ያሉት ግን ፈጣን ናቸው።

screens.title: Who moves faster?
screens.ask: Back on the merry-go-round: Hana near the centre, Dawit at the edge. Who moves faster in metres per second?
screens.after: Same angle each second, but Dawit's circle is bigger, so he covers more metres.

screens.title: Arc, speed and acceleration
paras: Arc length: s = rθ, with θ in radians.
The velocity is always along the tangent to the circle.
All points share ω and α. v and a grow with r.

notes.text: Example 2.5 asks for the average angular velocity but computes the angular acceleration (10 rad/s²). Average ω = (30 + 50)/2 = 40 rad/s. The lesson asks for both.
Example 2.7: the substitution squares α ("2 × (3 rad/s²)² × 628"). It should be 2 × 3 × 628. The answer 61.68 rad/s is right.
Example 2.10: 5 min = 300 s, not 3000 s. The answer 6.67 rev/s needs 300 s.
Example 2.12: the line "Δs = 0.4 m × 18 rad/s" should read v = 0.4 × 18.
Figure 2.10 label: the rotation shown is counterclockwise, not clockwise.
